lesson.title: The Lefty: Find Their Backhand
lesson.hook: Against a left-hander, your usual patterns land on their forehand. Turn them round.
lesson.tomorrow: Next time you play a lefty, say out loud before the first point: 'their backhand is on my left'.

pro.label: Is the lefty edge real?
pro.moment: Reviewing the research, Eng and Kovacs found the left-hander's advantage is small on the pro tour but can still exist at club level, and that it depends on how often you face lefties: practising against their patterns neutralises it.
pro.read: The lefty edge is unfamiliarity. Learn their patterns and it shrinks.
pro.src: ITF Coaching & Sport Science Review, Issue 63 (Aug 2014)

drill.name: Flip the pattern
drill.how: Rally with a left-hander, or a partner playing left-handed patterns. Score a point each time your ball lands on their backhand; lose one each time an inside-out forehand or a crosscourt backhand lands on their forehand.

steps.name: Running around your backhand
steps.sit: They're left-handed. You've run around your backhand to hit a forehand.
steps.payoff: Against a lefty, your inside-out forehand finds their forehand.
steps.principle: Their forehand is where your habits go. Turn them round.
steps.why: A lefty's forehand is on your right of their court, exactly where your inside-out forehand and your middle ball land. Inside-in goes to their backhand, and their reply is a rally ball.
steps.take: Lefty? Your inside-out lands on their forehand.

lines.A: Short and wide is their forehand too; they stretch for it: just in time.
lines.B: Right: inside-in, to their backhand. A rally ball back; you're in time.
lines.C: Your usual inside-out lands on their forehand: they attack; you're stretched.
lines.D: Through the middle is their forehand side too, and their forehand wins it.

steps.name: Their forehand, your backhand
steps.sit: Their crosscourt forehand keeps coming into your backhand corner.
steps.payoff: Crosscourt from your backhand corner feeds a lefty's forehand. Down the line finds their backhand.
steps.principle: Break the forehand-to-backhand rally by changing direction.
steps.why: From your backhand corner, crosscourt goes straight back to a lefty's forehand, and they keep the pressure on. Down the line reaches their backhand and takes the forehand out of the rally.
steps.take: Lefty pinning your backhand? Go down the line.

lines.A: Crosscourt slice lands on their forehand: they attack; you're in time.
lines.B: The middle reaches their backhand, but from the centre: you're in time.
lines.C: Right: down the line to their backhand. A rally ball back; you're set early.
lines.D: Crosscourt feeds their forehand again: they attack; you're just in time.

steps.name: Ad side, to a lefty
steps.sit: Second serve, ad side, to a left-handed returner standing in the usual spot.
steps.q: Where does your second serve go?
steps.payoff: On the ad side, a lefty's backhand is down the T, not out wide.
steps.principle: Find their backhand, wherever it is.
steps.why: Out wide on the ad side is a right-hander's backhand, but a lefty's forehand. At the body they take it on the forehand too. Down the T reaches their backhand, and the return is a rally ball.
steps.take: Ad side to a lefty? The T finds their backhand.

lines.A: Right: the T reaches their backhand. A rally ball back; you're in time.
lines.B: Wide is a lefty's forehand: they attack, and you're stretched.
lines.C: At the body they take it on the forehand: they attack; you're stretched.
lines.D: Slower and wide, straight to their forehand: they attack; you're stretched.
